title: Optimizing blue poo: A validated, cost-effective method for measuring whole gut transit time
author: Schmandt, Trunz, et al.
materials: capsule with rice crackers and liquid (see Table 1). A blue dye powder (Hollinger Farbpulver Blau, Günter Aroma AG, Beinwil, Switzerland) was used across all modes of delivery. The dye consisted of food colorants E131 (Patent Blue V) and E132 (Indigo Carmine) in a sodium chloride base, with a color concentration of 241 mg/g. The manufacturer’s recommended maximum daily intake corresponded to 1 g of dye powder, equivalent to 241 mg of food colorants. WGTT also varied depending on the dye concentration (Fig. 1). The highest concentration (241 mg) yielded a mean WGTT of 24 h 51 min (mean over all modes of delivery), while 120 mg resulted in 22 h 24 min. Notably, these high concentrations display that the capsule with liquid shortens mean transit time compared to other modes of delivery (Fig. 1). When the capsule with liquid data were excluded, the mean WGTT increased by approximately 2 h (241 mg: 26 h 28 min; 120 mg: 24 h 27 min), though this mean was based only on the two remaining modes of delivery. Furthermore, at these high concentrations, transit time was 25 % shorter for the capsule with liquid compared to the muffin, suggesting that co-ingestion with food mitigates the artificially fast transit observed with the capsule taken with liquid alone. Based on these findings, subsequent experiments minimized the amount of water consumed with the capsule and rice crackers to avoid replicating this accelerated transit effect.

steps.title: Gather all required materials
steps.instruction: Collect blue dye powder (Hollinger Farbpulver Blau, 241 mg g⁻¹, max daily intake 1 g = 241 mg colorant), vegetarian size‑1 capsules (0.68 mL, BIOVEA), agar‑agar, apple juice, gluten‑free rice crackers (M‑Classic Vollkornreiswaffeln), ingredients for vegan gluten‑free muffins (coconut yoghurt, oat milk, sugar, canola oil, vanilla paste, gluten‑free flour, baking powder), 200 mL and 100 mL water containers, a scale, measuring cylinders, mixing bowls, baking tray, oven, and a timer.

steps.title: Calculate dye amounts for each concentration
steps.instruction: Prepare four target colorant doses: 241 mg (100 % of max), 120 mg (50 %), 60 mg (25 %), and 30 mg (12.5 %). Because the powder contains 241 mg colorant per gram, weigh 1 g for 241 mg, 0.5 g for 120 mg, 0.25 g for 60 mg, and 0.125 g for 30 mg of dye powder.

steps.title: Fill capsules for liquid delivery
steps.instruction: For each concentration, load the calculated dye powder into vegetarian capsules (max 120 mg per capsule). Use two capsules for the 241 mg dose, one capsule for 120 mg, one capsule for 60 mg, and one capsule for 30 mg. Record that each capsule will be swallowed with 200 mL of water.

steps.title: Prepare gummy bears (two concentrations)
steps.instruction: Create two agar‑agar mixtures: (a) dissolve 4 g agar‑agar in 100 mL water, mix with 150 mL apple juice; each 10 mL bear will contain 60 mg colorant. (b) dissolve 2 g agar‑agar in 100 mL water, mix with 150 mL apple juice; each 10 mL bear will contain 30 mg colorant. Add the appropriate amount of dye powder to each batch to reach the target colorant per bear.

steps.title: Bake blue‑dye muffins
steps.instruction: Follow the published vegan, gluten‑free, lactose‑free muffin recipe (approx. 5 muffins ≈ 30 g each): 30 g coconut yoghurt, 30 g oat milk, 75 g sugar, 30 g canola oil, 7 g vanilla paste, 62.5 g gluten‑free flour, 2 g baking powder, and blue dye powder providing the required colorant (30 mg, 60 mg, 120 mg, or 241 mg) per muffin. Mix, portion, and bake each batch separately for each concentration.

steps.title: Assemble capsule with rice crackers
steps.instruction: Fill vegetarian capsules with the same four dye amounts (241 mg, 120 mg, 60 mg, 30 mg). Provide two gluten‑free rice crackers per dose. The participant will ingest the crackers, then the capsule, followed by 100 mL of water (≈ espresso cup).

steps.title: Schedule participant fasting and washout
steps.instruction: Ensure each participant observes an overnight fast of at least 8 hours (water only). Plan a minimum 2‑day washout between any two interventions to avoid residual dye interference. The study includes 14 interventions across the four delivery modes, with each participant completing a predefined subset.

steps.title: Administer the oral dose
steps.instruction: In the morning after the fast, give the participant the prepared dose according to the chosen mode: • Capsule with liquid – swallow the capsule(s) with 200 mL water. • Gummy bear – eat the bear with ≈200 mL water. • Muffin – eat the muffin with ≈200 mL water. • Capsule + rice crackers – eat two rice crackers, then the capsule, then 100 mL water.

steps.title: Record stool appearance times
steps.instruction: Participant notes the exact ingestion time, the time of the first blue‑colored stool, times of any subsequent blue stools, and the time of the first stool without visible blue coloration. All times are self‑reported.

steps.title: Calculate WGTT and assess visibility
steps.instruction: Compute whole‑gut transit time (WGTT) as the interval between ingestion and the first blue stool. Classify stool colour visibility as clearly visible, barely visible, or absent for each dose and delivery mode. Use these data to identify the optimal combination (capsule + rice crackers with 60 mg colorant).
